body.statement: Determine whether \(\mathfrak C_K\) can be completed into one arbitrary-\(\varepsilon\) validated certificate for the noncompact quotient values \(G_A(v_A,r_A)\), uniformly across all partial-tie faces, uniformly positive-definite covariance perturbations, and outer-design limits, while treating a vanishing action-relevant active rate through the proved infinite boundary value rather than evaluating a positive-rate Gaussian formula there.  The required theorem must prove that a screened hierarchical selector, which retains arms near the observed maximum and invokes compact selectors on every retained subset, uniformly approximates the unbounded game and transfers to the calibrated primitive experiments.  A radial truncation alone is not an admissible solution because configurations such as \((0,-a,-M)\) retain a lower-dimensional near-tie game as \(M\to\infty\).
body.justification: This isolates the genuinely open step needed for one design certificate before the analyst knows the active tie face.
body.gap: Neither Joo2025 nor Kato2026 proves the required static noncompact screened-selector approximation with changing faces and primitive exact-hit transfer.
body.consumer: A universal implementation would certify one outer design uniformly over partial ties and admissible covariance perturbations.
